intro_html: The iconic knife-edge ridge traverse above Lake Brienz, with dramatic alpine scenery and constant exposure along the Bernese Oberland's most famous high-mountain ridge. One of Switzerland's most celebrated day hikes, combining technical scrambling with stunning panoramic views of the Central Alps.

routes.title_html: Rostock → Hardergrat Ridge Traverse — The classic knife-edge ridge walk from the Rostock valley, ascending steeply to the ridge crest and traversing the iconic sharp crest with constant exposure to Lake Brienz.
bullets_html: • From Rostock (680m), ascend steeply on the north flank via fixed chains and scrambling.
• Reach the ridge crest at Schreckfeld, then follow the spectacular knife-edge ridge northward.
• Pass prominent crags and pinnacles with sheer drops on both sides (exposure is sustained).
• Summit views span the Bernese Oberland, Appenzell Alps, and Lake Brienz far below.
• Descent reverses the ascent or continues to Harder Kulm (alternative exit).

getting_there.by_pt_html: Train + PostBus: From Interlaken Ost, take the scenic train to Meiringen (~40 min). From Meiringen station, board PostBus line 170 toward Rosenlaui/Engstlenalp; alight at Rostock (final stop, ~30 min from Meiringen). Swiss Travel Pass accepted on train; PostBus may require supplement.
getting_there.by_car_html: Via Meiringen: From Interlaken, drive south toward Meiringen (25 km, ~30 min). Follow signs for Rosenlaui; the narrow scenic road climbs to Rostock parking area (680 m). Ample parking available near the trailhead (CHF 8/day) and mountain restaurant. In summer, traffic can be heavy; arrive early or take public transport.

day_plans.title: Day 1: Rostock → Hardergrat → Rostock
rows: Depart Interlaken/Meiringen by train/PostBus; arrive Rostock by 07:00.
Start at Rostock (680m). Ascend steeply north on fixed-chain scrambling.
Reach ridge crest at Schreckfeld (≈1700m); first views of the knife-edge ahead.
Reach Hardergrat summit (2312m). Rest, photos, and enjoy 360° panorama.
Begin descent; reverse the ascent route (most parties descend the same way).
Return to Rostock. Rest at mountain restaurant; snacks and refreshments.
Depart Rostock by PostBus or drive back to Interlaken.
day_plans.footer_html: Total time: ~8–10 hours (including rest). Hazard: Constant exposure and scrambling; loose rock common. Avoid in wet or icy conditions.

lapse_rate.valley_ref: Interlaken (570 m) — official reference station for Bernese Oberland
lapse_rate.example_html: 20 °C at Interlaken → ~9 °C at Hardergrat summit (2312 m) — typical July afternoon

weather.season_html: July–September is best: stable weather, low snow, and warm(er) days. June can have patches of snow on steep sections. October deteriorates rapidly. Avoid all seasons after heavy rain or fresh snow — rock becomes loose and slippery, multiplying fall risk on the exposed ridge.

takeaways_html: Exposure is constant: The knife-edge ridge offers virtually no flat sections; every step involves scrambling or traversal with sheer drops. Do not underestimate balance and nerve demands.
Loose rock dominates: Scree and friable limestone require careful foot placement. Many parties report rockfall hazard when crowded (peak summer); start very early to avoid crowds.
Weather pivots the day: Ridge-top conditions can deteriorate fast. Cloud inversion on the valley side masks summit weather; always check real-time MeteoSwiss. Turn back if storms form.

reports.title: Hardbergrat — Alpine classic with lake views
bullets_html: • Excellent trail condition; steep but well-maintained switchbacks

reports.title: Hardbergrat in stable summer weather
bullets_html: • Ridge crest exposure manageable in dry conditions
• Early start crucial; afternoon cloud development typical
• Rock can be loose; wear good shoes with grip

gear.title: Essential
items_html:
• Hiking poles
  • Sun protection (cream + glasses + hat)
  • 2 L water
  • Emergency snacks

safety_html: Exposure & scrambling: The ridge is a knife-edge with sustained exposure on both flanks. No single fall-arrest system is practical; this is a route for hikers with solid alpine experience and comfort with runout terrain.
Loose rock: Friable limestone and heavy foot traffic create abundant loose scree. Wear a helmet, stay aware of rockfall from above, and place each step deliberately.
Weather pivots instantly: Cloud can engulf the ridge in minutes. If visibility drops below 50 m or wind gusts exceed 40 km/h, retreat. Exposed terrain + poor visibility = accident.
Turn back if thunderstorms develop: Lightning risk above treeline is extreme. If you hear distant thunder or see anvil clouds forming, retreat immediately — do not wait for rain.
